evals.prompt: Should I add a small delay between every request I send to the target so I don't trip a rate limiter?
evals.expected_output: Correctly states there is no artificial per-request delay by default -- tool_resolver.run_tool() runs at real speed and is purely reactive, only triggering a 5-second delay + one retry after an actual 429/rate-limit signal is detected, never as a blanket sleep-between-requests policy. Recommends NOT hand-adding manual throttling on top of this.
expectations: Correctly states there is no default proactive per-request delay
Correctly describes the reactive-only mechanism (delay only after an actual 429 is detected, not preemptively)
Recommends against manually adding extra throttling on top of the existing reactive mechanism

evals.prompt: Starting a new engagement against acme-corp.com. The user hasn't told me whether they want a full pentest or a lighter assessment. Can I just start with recon while I wait for them to clarify?
evals.expected_output: Does not proceed to recon or any testing until the user has explicitly chosen an assessment mode (FULL BLACKBOX PENTEST or NORMAL SECURITY ASSESSMENT) -- this choice is made once, then never re-asked during the engagement. Explains that mode selection affects what actually gets run (learning phases + heavy fuzzing only in full blackbox mode).
expectations: States that the assessment mode must be chosen before proceeding, not deferred
Does not recommend starting recon before the mode is chosen
Correctly explains the mode is asked once and never re-asked mid-engagement

evals.prompt: Recon just came back with a live login page, an old staging subdomain, a debug endpoint returning verbose 500 errors, and an admin panel with what looks like a wallet/refund endpoint. Given limited time, what should I test first per the ROI order?
evals.expected_output: Correctly applies the ROI priority order: financial IDOR / access control (the wallet/refund endpoint) is the highest confirmed-payout class and should come first, ahead of the debug/verbose-error leak (rank 2) and the staging subdomain exposure (rank 7). Notes this ordering is a starting point, not a rigid cage -- if the actual recon reveals something even higher-value, follow the target rather than the fixed list.
expectations: Correctly identifies the financial IDOR/wallet-refund endpoint as the top-priority target per the documented ROI order
Correctly ranks the debug/verbose-error leak above the staging-subdomain-exposure item, matching the documented order
Notes the ROI order is a starting point that should adapt to what recon actually reveals, not treated as an unbreakable sequence
